title: Conventional Comments Toolkit — repository configuration
description: Schema for .conventional-comments.json, read from a repository's default branch by conventional-comments-toolkit. Transcribed from packages/core/src/config/schema.ts; the validator in that file remains authoritative. Unknown keys are ignored with a warning at runtime — this schema flags them so you see them while editing. That includes the keys retired with the verifier, which the extension no longer reads: formatSeverity, overrideLabel, resolverOverrideGroup, activation, docUrl, server and exemptionLog.

$schema.description: URL of this schema. Editors use it for completion and validation.

version.description: Configuration schema version. A document declaring a version above the one the extension supports is not applied: the extension falls back to assist mode, or to the floor if the floor is stricter. Highest version supported today: 1.

mode.description: off — nothing happens. assist — the extension helps and diagnoses, and never blocks. enforce — the extension refuses to send a non-compliant comment, in the browser of whoever has it installed. No mode ever blocks a merge: the extension reports unresolved blocking threads, it does not gate completion. See the adoption guide for what these modes mean in practice.

anyOf.deprecationMessage: "warn" is obsolete: the extension reads it as "assist" and shows a configuration notice. Write "assist".
anyOf.description: Obsolete. Still accepted, and read as assist with a configuration notice.

labels.description: Per-label overrides, and labels of your own. Only the keys you list are overridden; every other label keeps its product default. Nineteen labels ship: the twelve of Conventional Comments, and seven added by the toolkit. All are enabled by default except quibble.

id.description: Label identifier, always in English — it is a grammar token, not translatable text.

enabled.description: Whether the label may be used in this repository. Every shipped label is enabled by default except quibble, which Conventional Comments itself defines as a nitpick under another name. This key, and it alone, turns off the labels the toolkit adds to Conventional Comments: summary, reviewed, thanks, done, ack and disagree.

blockingByDefault.description: Whether a comment carrying this label blocks when no decoration forces otherwise. True by default for issue, todo and chore.

alwaysNonBlocking.description: Whether the label can never block. A (blocking) decoration on such a label raises E-CONFLICT, and the verdict falls back to blockingByDefault. True by default for nitpick, thought, note and for the seven labels the toolkit adds.

kind.description: What the label does with a point. remark — it raises one. reply — it answers one. status — it does neither, and says where the review stands. The kind decides which row of the toolbar the button sits in, and keeps status and reply labels out of the statistics computed on remarks. It never changes a verdict. Default: the shipped kind for a shipped label, remark for a label you declare.

icon.description: Emoji shown on the button and the badge. Purely cosmetic: it never changes a verdict.

color.description: Badge border colour, conventionally #rrggbb. The validator only checks that this is a string, so the schema does not reject other forms either: a transcription that refuses what the product accepts is not a transcription. It only ever touches border-color, never a background at rest — so the applicable contrast criterion is WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11 (3:1 for a UI component boundary), not the 4.5:1 required of text. Cosmetic: it never changes a verdict.

description.description: What the label means, shown as the tooltip of the badge — and of the button when usage is absent. Shown as written, whatever the interface language. Written, it replaces the shipped text; written empty (""), it removes the tooltip; left out, a shipped label keeps its text. Never changes a verdict.

usage.description: When to use the label, shown as the tooltip of the button. Written, it replaces the shipped text and its example; written empty (""), it removes the button's tooltip; left out, the button shows description, then the shipped text. Never changes a verdict.

aliases.description: Alternative spellings accepted for this label on input: with "bug" as an alias of issue, bug: is read as issue: and inherits everything from it. An alias raises no diagnostic; the extension may offer to rewrite it to the canonical form, and never requires it.

decorations.description: The words allowed in parentheses after a label.

allowFree.description: Whether decorations outside the known list are accepted. They are rendered and counted, and never affect the verdict. Set false to raise E-UNKNOWN-DECORATION on anything unlisted.

known.description: Decorations whose effect on the verdict is defined.

forces.description: blocking — the comment blocks. non-blocking — it does not. null — no effect on the verdict; the decoration carries meaning for humans only.

severities.description: Re-level or silence individual diagnostics. Errors make a comment non-compliant; warnings are shown, never a cause of failure. Codes not listed here keep their product severity, and an unrecognised code is accepted without complaint. Two limits apply at runtime, each reported by a configuration notice: an E- code never goes below warn, and W-SESSION-MULTIPLE never goes above it.

E-MALFORMED-PREFIX.description: A prefix that nearly parses, but does not.

E-UNKNOWN-LABEL.description: Label not enabled in this repository.

E-UNKNOWN-DECORATION.description: Unknown decoration while decorations.allowFree is false.

E-DECISION-SUBJECT.description: A decision reply shorter than rules.minDecisionSubjectLength.

W-CASE.description: Wrong casing. Ships a one-click fix.

W-DECORATION-STYLE.description: Spacing or ordering off. Ships a one-click fix.

W-SUBJECT-TOO-SHORT.description: Shorter than rules.minSubjectLength. Deliberately a warning at a low threshold.

W-MISSING-DECORATION.description: suggestion or question written with no decoration — the two labels whose blocking intent cannot be guessed.

W-NO-DISCUSSION.description: A blocking comment with no discussion under it.

W-NOT-BLOCKABLE.description: A blocking comment in a place that cannot carry that state.

W-SESSION-MULTIPLE.description: More than one review-session marker in a comment. Never above warn: "error" is read as warn, so that a metadata mistake can never block a send.

scope.description: Which parts of a pull request are validated.

validateReplies.description: Whether replies inside a thread are validated. Even when false, a reply whose resolved label is decision is still read — otherwise the rule on its subject would only apply in repositories that had opted into validating replies.

validateReviewSummary.description: Whether a review's overall body is validated. An empty body is exempt regardless: an Approve with no text must never fail.

minSubjectLength.description: Below this, W-SUBJECT-TOO-SHORT. Deliberately a warning and a low threshold: making it blocking pushes people to work around the rule rather than apply it.

minDecisionSubjectLength.description: Minimum length of a decision reply, and the only length threshold that applies to it. Below it, E-DECISION-SUBJECT — an error, not a warning: setting a remark aside requires a sentence saying why.

exemptUsers.description: Authors whose comments are never validated, compared against the platform login, case-insensitively — never the display name.

allowlistPatterns.description: Regular expressions matched against the whole trimmed comment body. A match exempts the comment. Beyond the bounds this schema can express (50 patterns, 256 characters), an entry is also rejected at runtime if it is not a valid regular expression, or if it contains a nested quantifier — the shape behind most known ReDoS.

toolCommands.description: Comments addressed to a bot rather than to a human. EMPTY BY DEFAULT: in enforce mode a bare /rebase is rejected like any other comment until the repository adds "/*". Two forms are accepted: "/*", which exempts every slash command at the start of a body, and an exact bot handle such as "@dependabot". A single slash command cannot be exempted on its own: an entry such as "/rebase" is ignored at runtime, with a configuration notice. Each entry is compared literally, never interpreted as a pattern.

oneOf.description: Sentinel enabling generic recognition of any slash command at the start of a body.
An exact bot handle. Matched on the whole first token, case-insensitively.

configUrl.description: URL of the organization configuration document. ONLY MEANINGFUL AT ORGANIZATION LEVEL: set in a repository file it is ignored and reported, because the organization URL comes exclusively from the floor channel.

coreMinVersion.description: Minimum core/ version required to apply this document. Only the MAJOR component is compared with the extension's core major: on a 1.x core, "1.99.0" is applied and "2.0.0" is not — the extension then falls back to assist mode, or to the floor if stricter. It cannot require a newer minor or patch release.

configCacheTtlSeconds.description: How long the extension caches a resolved configuration, in seconds. What it displays may lag by up to that long. Blocking does not: before it refuses to send a comment, the extension re-reads the configuration without its cache. An organization's policy can set a maximum; a repository may ask for less.

badgeStyle.description: Badge shape. Two values are styled: "pill" and "flat". Any other string is accepted but renders unstyled. Cosmetic: it never changes a verdict.

sessionIcon.description: Icon of the mention that replaces a review-session marker — a line [session:<id>] — when a comment is displayed. Never changes a verdict.

shortcuts.description: Keyboard expansions in the comment editor.

abbreviations.description: Maps an abbreviation to the text it expands to. Defaults use as many letters as needed to be unambiguous: ?i, ?ib, ?ni, ?no, ?que, ?qui…

language.description: Language of descriptions and messages. Anything not starting with fr resolves to en. Label identifiers stay in English regardless — they are grammar tokens, not text.

telemetry.description: Disabled by default. No comment, code or diff content is ever sent, whatever this is set to.

severity.description: off — the diagnostic is not raised. warn — reported, never blocking. error — makes the comment non-compliant.
